clue.text: Reception by Gore Vidal

definitions.meaning: a social gathering held in one's house to receive guests
the title of a 1988 essay collection by the American writer Gore Vidal

explanation.definitionFit: A party held for callers in a private house is so named, and Vidal used the same phrase as a book title.

clue.text: Schubert quintet in new version for teacher ()

indicators.note: a new version of something is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Schubert's Piano Quintet in A is known as the Trout

explanation.surface: A fresh arrangement of a famous chamber work is made for a music teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is indirect: first name the quintet, the Trout, then 'in new version' rearranges TROUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A private instructor is a synonym for a teacher.

clue.text: "The very best -the -— that you keep for your own drinking, Jack!" (Barnaby Rudge)

definitions.text: "The very best -the -— that you keep for your own drinking, Jack!" (Barnaby Rudge)

parts.words: "The very best -the -— that you keep for your own drinking, Jack!" (Barnaby Rudge)
parts.note: a quotation from Dickens with a blank: the missing hyphenated word describes spirits stronger than the standard measure

explanation.walkthrough: The solver fills the gap in Dickens's line from Barnaby Rudge, where the innkeeper is asked for his strongest spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit above the standard alcoholic strength is the very best kept for the landlord's own drinking.

clue.text: Lamb lovers, and possibly devotees of roast pork

definitions.meaning: admirers of Charles Lamb, who wrote as Elia
Lamb's essay A Dissertation upon Roast Pig might make his fans fond of that dish

explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb's pen name was Elia, so his admirers take that name, and his famous essay praises crackling pig.

clue.text: Tale-telling freeholder

parts.note: a medieval landowner below the gentry who tells one of the stories on Chaucer's pilgrimage

explanation.walkthrough: In Chaucer's Canterbury Tales one pilgrim is a free landholder of this rank who tells his own tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval freeholder was a landowner of this class, and Chaucer's pilgrim of that rank tells a tale.

clue.text: Bolt piece inspired by Housman line?

definitions.meaning: a play by the English dramatist Robert Bolt
Housman's poem begins 'Loveliest of trees, the cherry now', describing a tree in blossom

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Bolt's 1957 play has this title, and a blossoming tree is what Housman's famous poem celebrates.

clue.text: A river chart, avoided by wily plagiarist

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
a graph is a chart of data

explanation.surface: A map of a river is something a cunning copier steers clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a wily plagiarist would avoid an exact transcript, since a word-for-word copy is easily spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a copy or transcript of an original document, which a clever plagiarist would not produce.

clue.text: Poet takes off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was an English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Antiquary's recorded by Hearne

parts.note: Thomas Hearne published the travel notes of the Tudor antiquary John Leland

explanation.walkthrough: John Leland, Henry VIII's antiquary, wrote an account of his journeys round England; Thomas Hearne edited and printed it in the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Leland's record of his travels through England is known by this word for a route or journey log.

clue.text: Persist too clumsily and boisterously

indicators.note: something done clumsily is done awkwardly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going too awkwardly and noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsily' rearranges PERSIST and TOO; the answer is an Italian musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction means to be played in a noisy, boisterous manner.

clue.text: Partial conjugation of to be" for novelist

parts.note: two present forms of the verb: first person singular
the third person singular present form of the verb

explanation.surface: A grammar exercise in the verb is offered to a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley and Martin are both well-known English novelists of that surname.

clue.text: "The daring pleasure of youth as yet undaunted by any previous fall ", he said (Surtees)

definitions.text: "The daring pleasure of youth as yet undaunted by any previous fall ", he said (Surtees)

parts.words: "The daring pleasure of youth as yet undaunted by any previous fall ", he said (Surtees)
parts.note: a line from R S Surtees, whose hunting novels follow a sporting adventurer on tour; the speaker is that character

explanation.walkthrough: The solver must identify which Surtees character speaks the quoted line; it is the hero of his hunting novel about a sporting tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Surtees's hard-riding title character in a novel of 1853 is the speaker of this line about fearless hunting youth.

clue.text: American humorist — translator of Nestor

indicators.note: a translator turns words into a new form, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American comic writer turned out to have rendered the Homeric sage into English.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Rosten, author of The Joys of Yiddish, was an American humorist.

clue.text: Some prize not intended for Stoic

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of an award was not meant for a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'intended for Stoic' as the definition, but only 'Stoic' defines; 'intended for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeno of Citium founded the Stoic school of philosophy in Athens.

clue.text: European movement by a student is strongly felt

parts.note: motion is movement
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A European protest march by a student stirs deep feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emotional is charged with feeling, felt keenly.

clue.text: Endanger article in large book

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other here

parts.note: to imperil is to endanger
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Putting an item in a big volume puts it at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial is a traditional large paper size, so a book of that format is a big one.

clue.text: Always mention how old the victim was? (As Boot may have learned from Corker)

definitions.text: Always mention how old the victim was? (As Boot may have learned from Corker)

parts.words: Always mention how old the victim was? (As Boot may have learned from Corker)
parts.note: split, the word gives an instruction to state the age; in Waugh's Scoop the veteran Corker teaches the novice William Boot newspaper work

explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the word reads as a newspaper rule to report the age; whole, it means journalism, which Boot learns from Corker in Evelyn Waugh's Scoop.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalistic reporting of events is what Corker teaches Boot in Scoop.

clue.text: Sailor on most of arachnophobe's seat is a hypocrite

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Little Miss Muffet, frightened away by a spider, sat on a tuffet

explanation.surface: A seaman perched on most of a spider-fearer's stool is two-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: The arachnophobe is Miss Muffet of the nursery rhyme; 'most of' drops the final T of TUFFET to leave TUFFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière's Tartuffe is a religious hypocrite, and his name now means one.

clue.text: Friends of Mowgli on first-name terms with composer?

definitions.meaning: the boy in Kipling's Jungle Book is raised by a pack of wolves
Mozart's first name, used by someone familiar with him

explanation.definitionFit: Mowgli's companions form a wolf pack, and Mozart's given name read as two words gives the same.

clue.text: Box with new content for assembly hill

indicators.note: the content of something is what is inside it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a pyx is a box, especially one for the consecrated bread

explanation.surface: A container gets fresh contents for a hill where people meet.
explanation.definitionFit: The hill in ancient Athens where the citizens' assembly met.

clue.text: Those of Corbiere were distinctly uneasy

definitions.text: Those of Corbiere were distinctly uneasy

parts.words: Those of Corbiere were distinctly uneasy
parts.note: the French poet Tristan Corbière's only collection is Les ___ jaunes, the yellow loves, yellow suggesting forced, uneasy laughter

explanation.walkthrough: Corbière's book Les Amours jaunes has 'jaune' in the sense of a sickly, forced laugh, so his love affairs were uneasy ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for love affairs forms the title of Corbière's collection.

clue.text: Young even-toed ungulate seen in company of sweet-toothed carnivore

definitions.meaning: a young pig; pigs are cloven-hoofed mammals

definitions.text: seen in company of sweet-toothed carnivore
definitions.meaning: the small companion of the honey-loving bear Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.definitionFit: A baby swine is so called, and A A Milne's small friend of the honey-mad bear has that name.

clue.text: He made a single for William F. Nolan?

definitions.text: He made a single for William F. Nolan?

parts.words: He made a single for William F. Nolan?
parts.note: Nolan co-wrote a novel whose hero makes a famous run, and a single is a run in cricket

explanation.walkthrough: William F. Nolan co-wrote Logan's Run; in cricket a single is one run, so the hero 'made a single'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of the novel Logan's Run is the man whose run gives the book its title.

clue.text: Fatal flaw in classic drama

parts.note: Aristotle's term for the error or weakness that brings down a tragic hero

explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle's Poetics names the tragic hero's error or failing that leads to his downfall.

clue.text: Where to place remains, Browne tells us Correction: Two clues were omitted from the Down section of Crossword 605 (June 10). They were:

definitions.text: Where to place remains, Browne tells us

parts.words: Where to place remains, Browne tells us
parts.note: Sir Thomas Browne's Urn Burial discusses putting ashes into a vessel

explanation.walkthrough: The text after 'tells us' is a newspaper correction notice printed beside the clue, not part of it. Read as two words, the answer says where ashes go.
explanation.definitionFit: To put cremated ashes into a funerary vessel, the subject of Browne's Hydriotaphia, Urn Burial.

clue.text: Comfortable theatrical joiner

definitions.meaning: the joiner among Shakespeare's mechanicals in A Midsummer Night's Dream, who plays the Lion

explanation.definitionFit: Cosy means much the same, and Shakespeare's carpenter who plays the lion bears this name.

clue.text: Dekker protagonist reveals Faust to run indefinitely

indicators.note: indefinitely suggests no fixed form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dramatist's hero shows that Faust will keep running forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indefinitely' rearranges FAUST and TO RUN; Thomas Dekker wrote Old Fortunatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Dekker's play Old Fortunatus is named after its hero, the man with the magic purse.

clue.text: Singer dramatically presented by him

parts.note: the playwright Peter of this surname wrote the stage play Singer, about a refugee racketeer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is not a vocalist but the title of a 1989 play; its author is the dramatist Peter Flannery.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Flannery is the English dramatist who wrote Singer for the RSC.

clue.text: Unbending writer back East?

parts.note: stern means unbending, severe
back says the next piece goes at the end

explanation.surface: A severe author returns to the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the author of Tristram Shandy.
